changes.summary: Initial build-kit release.

Pressed and open menu-bar headings keep their size and are drawn as a flat navy highlight with white text and an unmoved label, not sunken (GUI95's reading of the Windows 95 menu bar, not a cited source); menu items no longer sink when pressed; check and option marks and the submenu arrow are pixel artwork in the item colour (marks embossed when unavailable) with no generated text, so the marks stay out of the accessible name and do not depend on a symbol font. Shared stylesheet: the scope root is in the border-box reset; check boxes, option buttons, drop-down lists, up-down controls, sliders, progress bars, list boxes, property tabs and scrollbars are drawn by the stylesheet; the verifier also runs a new period lint, and a stored state-atlas image checks what the stylesheet paints.

No change to this control or to the stylesheet's rules. Period lint: elements at opacity 0 (their own or an ancestor's) count as hidden; the shapes inside an SVG image are image content and are not judged, though the svg element is; a drop-down the page draws itself with appearance: base-select is not a native-control finding; and a new control-text-size rule reports buttons, labels, fields, drop-down lists, legends, menu items and tabs whose text is not 11px, once against the outermost element that sets the size. A page that passed the 1.1.0 lint can fail this one on text size.

No change to this control's behaviour or to the runtime. Shared stylesheet: every two-line edge now gives the bottom and right lines the top-right and bottom-left corner pixels, as Windows draws them; windows, dialogs, pop-up menus, scroll bar arrows and thumb and spin arrows take a new plain raised edge, --gui95-raised-plain (light gray outside, white inside), while push buttons and tab pages keep --gui95-raised; a held or latched push button takes a new --gui95-pressed edge (black outside, gray inside) in place of the field's sunken edge; a pressed default button keeps its black frame and shows one gray line round a flat face. Arrangements taken from the edge-drawing code of Wine and ReactOS and a border diagram in Howlett's Visual Interface Design for Windows, not from a Windows 95 screenshot. A page that draws its own window with --gui95-raised keeps the button edge until it switches to --gui95-raised-plain. The state atlas baseline is regenerated.

Arrow keys, Home and End now stop on unavailable commands (only separators are skipped) and Enter, Space and mnemonics do nothing there; shortcut text is left-aligned in one column per menu; a submenu opens after the pointer rests 400 ms on its parent and at once from the keyboard or a press. Shared stylesheet and kit: opt-in dialog layout attributes (data-gui95-dialog-layout, -dialog-body, -buttons, -form, -stack, -row, -fill, -group, -page) built on two dialog-unit custom properties, with the 7-unit margin, 4-unit gap, 14-unit control height and 50-unit command button of the final 1995 guidelines; a density switch, data-gui95-density="period", giving the sizes measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5) on 19 November 2026 (17 px menu commands, 18 px title bar, 13 px list rows, 21 px closed drop-down list) while "comfortable", the default, keeps the previous sizes; check boxes and option buttons show a face-coloured interior while held and take the focus rectangle round the label text; a focused closed drop-down list highlights its text area only; unavailable drop-down and up-down arrows are engraved; a group box caption interrupts the white line as well as the shadow line; the slider thumb's corners follow the edge rule; the default push button's black frame is inside the button's own box. New warn-only lints, lint-wording and lint-layout, and a register of 190 period rules (kit/evidence/register.json). Existing selectors keep their comfortable metrics; a page that relied on a default button painting one pixel outside its box, or on arrow keys skipping unavailable menu commands, will see a difference. Checked against a capture of real Windows 95: 21 of 54 compared control states match pixel for pixel at 24-bit.

No change to menu behaviour. Shared stylesheet and kit: the period density now also gives the sizes and drawing measured on Windows 95 for the tree (16 px rows, 19 px a level, a 9 px plus or minus box, dotted lines on Windows' pixels), the up-down control (two 15 by 9 px buttons one pixel apart, 3 by 2 px arrows), the slider thumb (pointed, the channel 7 px below its top, not drawn when unavailable), a list box the browser draws (13 px rows starting at the frame), and the toolbar inset; the comfortable sizes are unchanged. Two layout values are new in both densities: data-gui95-dialog-layout="sheet" frames a property sheet with 4 dialog units, and data-gui95-buttons="wizard" sets Back and Next edge to edge with Cancel 10 px away; the layout lint accepts both margins. In a dialog the default-button frame follows the focus to whichever push button has it, as on Windows 95. caption-controls.css draws 16 by 14 px buttons with Windows' marks in the period density, and its resting edge gives the corner pixels to the dark lines in both densities; an application that copied the file needs the new copy. A page using the period density will look different in these controls; the period atlas baseline was regenerated and the comfortable one is unchanged.
